messages:
incident-bot: [P1] Canary rollout memory/throttle alert for inference-runtime-v2 in eu-west-1. 6/8 canary pods reporting OOMKilled or cpu throttling, autoscaler paused the rollout. Auto-pause reason: pod failures > 30% within 10m. Link: https://infra.redwood/alerts/ALRT-3821

jamie: I'm on it — pulling logs and metrics now. Any customer-facing impact?

incident-bot: No active 5xx surge in the global LB yet, but latency for embeddings endpoint +90% in eu-west-1. Error types: OOMKilled and container runtime SIGKILLs.

sara: checking k8s, looks like memory requests were lowered in the canary spec compared to previous stable. rollout@v2.7.0 -> canary v2.8.0. Patch shows new kernel runtime + dynamic quantization lib.

diego: that new kernel (new_kernel_opt) introduced a memory regression in a perf test yesterday, flagged but marked as low-prob. Guess it hit production.

jamie: can we pause the rollout fully and scale down canary to zero? I don't want traffic funneling to failing pods.

sara: pausing rollout now via kubectl: ```
kubectl -n inference patch deployment inference-runtime-v2 -p '{"spec":{"paused":true}}'
kubectl -n inference scale deployment inference-runtime-v2-canary --replicas=0
```

sara: done — rollout paused, canary pods scaled to 0. Confirming no new canary pods are created.

mike: product — any active customers routed to canary? We had a small traffic split (5%) for canary. If rollout paused, traffic should revert to stable.

jamie: traffic steering executed: route rule removed, all traffic now to stable v2.7.0. I'll watch for request backs and latency. :eyes:

diego: collecting the failing pod logs — sample from pod inference-runtime-v2-canary-5f2b: ```
[2026-03-15T02:37:12Z] oom_killer invoked: task inference_main killed
[2026-03-15T02:37:12Z] runtime: SIGKILL due to memory cgroup limit
stack: ...
model_loader: alloc 3.2GB -> failed
quant_cache: reserve 1.5GB -> failed
```

diego: it looks like memory reservation for the new kernel went up ~30% for large sequences. Autoscaler min/max are fine but the container requests are too low for the new binary.

jamie: action list so far: 1) paused rollout 2) scaled canary -> 0 3) rerouted traffic 4) collecting logs/metrics 5) notify SRE & infra. Anything else?

incident-bot: Paging oncall escalation to next: @oncall-2 (pager).

oncall-2: acknowledging. Picking this up. Was there a feature flag involved for the kernel switch?

diego: yes, config flag: `feature:inference_runtime.kernel_switch=v2_opt`. The rollout included flipping that flag + updated image. Canary was the first place it flipped.

oncall-2: can we flip the flag back globally as a fast kill-switch instead of full rollback? If the flag is server-side we can revert without image rollbacks.

mike: product: the flag is client-side baked into image, not a remote toggle. We can only kill the rollout or rollback the image.

jamie: in that case the quickest low-risk path is rollback the canary image to stable, then do a safe rollout with adjusted requests or kernel tweaks.

sara: how about bumping memory requests on the new image and re-run canary with smaller traffic? That avoids rollback but requires a new build and deployment. Might take 20-30m.

diego: I prefer rollback for immediate mitigation, then we reintroduce with memory bump. We should also run a quick memory soak test on a staging cluster.

jamie: agree. rolling back the canary image to v2.7.0 now and then scaling back to typical canary replica count for a short smoke test.

sara: rollback commands: ```
kubectl -n inference set image deployment/inference-runtime-v2-canary inference-runtime=registry.redwood/inference:v2.7.0
kubectl -n inference rollout status deployment/inference-runtime-v2-canary
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/inference-runtime-v2-canary --replicas=2
```

sara: applied. Waited for pods to come up — both stable-image pods are running. Smoke test run against canary OK, memory stable.

jamie: customer impact: small ~5% exposure window while traffic was steered; about 120 requests failed with OOMs over the 6-minute window. No major customers reported data loss. Notifying trust & safety and support with NRT summary.

mike: please log customer-facing summary and estimated ETA for full re-rollout. Product expects a postmortem.

diego: root cause preliminary: new_kernel_opt increases per-request memory for long contexts; memory requests in k8s manifest weren't updated. Repro steps added to infra issue INFRA-4493.

jamie: handoff: oncall-2, I'll hand this to you for the next 6 hours — keep tracking any regression when we start a new canary once we have patched image or bumped requests. Checklist in the thread: 
- monitor eu-west-1 latency and 5xx
- run staging memory soak with new image for 30m before canary
- update k8s manifest memory requests for new image
- coordinate with product for rollout comms

oncall-2: acknowledged. I'll take post-rollback monitoring and lead re-introduction plan. If we need to enable a temporary rate limit for long sequences I can patch the ingress rules.

sara: created infra ticket INFRA-4493 with logs and a patch proposal. Tagging @diego for kernel investigation.

mike: will prep the product communication and escalation notes. No customer escalations yet, but we'll send an FYI to the top 10 customers routed through eu-west-1.

jamie: closing immediate page — canary mitigated and traffic stable. Leaving thread open for postmortem; will dump perf metrics and timeline here later. :white_check_mark:

oncall-2: taking ownership for the postmortem. Next update in 2 hours or earlier if anything changes.

incident-bot: Incident status changed: mitigated -> monitoring. Ticket: INC-3821.
